fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. John says, "With righteousness He judges and wages war." (Revelation 19:11) Righteousness is the way He judges and the way He wages war. I can't say the same about my first batch of the morning.

Cunning sounds like a villain's word, doesn't it? John never uses it for this rider. He says, "With righteousness He judges and wages war." (Revelation 19:11) The rider is called Faithful and True, and righteousness is the word John names.

True, baker. John says, "He has a name written on Him that only He Himself knows." (Revelation 19:12) So there's a name on Him that only He knows. I have "Dorin" carved in my handle, and that one is no secret.
Right, baker. The armies of heaven "…follow Him on white horses." (Revelation 19:14) They ride behind the rider, not ahead of Him. So He is in front and they come behind Him.

That's it, friend. John says they are "…dressed in fine linen, white and pure…" (Revelation 19:14) They follow the rider on white horses in that clothing. White clothes on white horses, and I'd be nervous bringing my flour-dusted apron anywhere near that parade.

Armor makes sense when you picture an army, I get it. But John doesn't say that. The armies of heaven are "…dressed in fine linen, white and pure…" (Revelation 19:14) That's the clothing the text names for them.

Sackcloth and ashes is a very different look, friend. John says the armies are "…dressed in fine linen, white and pure…" (Revelation 19:14) That's the clothing the text names for them. White and pure is a look my apron gave up on years ago.
Yes, baker. The sword is "…with which to strike down the nations…" (Revelation 19:15) John says it proceeds from His mouth. So the nations are who the sword is for.

Yes, baker. The angel "…cried out in a loud voice to all the birds flying overhead…" (Revelation 19:17) So his message goes to the birds. He is calling them to gather for what he names the great supper of God.

The twenty-four elders aren't who the angel is calling, friend. John says the angel "…cried out in a loud voice to all the birds flying overhead…" (Revelation 19:17) No elders are named in this passage. The birds are the audience for this one.

Right, baker. The angel's list goes on past kings, commanders and mighty men to "…horses and riders, of everyone slave and free, small and great." (Revelation 19:18) So the list doesn't stop where the question says it does. It reaches well past the kings, commanders and mighty men.

The seven churches aren't named in this part, friend. John says the beast and the kings assembled "…to wage war against the One seated on the horse, and against His army." (Revelation 19:19) The One on the horse and His army are who they face. The seven churches don't come up in these verses.

That's it, baker. John says the false prophet, "…on its behalf had performed signs deceiving those who had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image." (Revelation 19:20) So he used signs to deceive people. I think this one is heavy.
